name: China economy
summary: China's property investment fell 21.6% in the first ten months and retail sales grew 0.4% in October; slump persists
state: China's statistics bureau reported on 16 Nov that real estate development investment fell 21.6% year on year in January–October, new home floor space sold fell 13.7%, and October retail sales rose only 0.4% (NBS). GDP grew 4.6% in the first three quarters, within the 4.5–5% target, helped by exports up 35.2% in October (China Briefing). The prolonged property slump keeps Watch; no hard landing below 3% growth, financial contagion or sharp capital-control tightening was found as of 27 Nov.
for_you: Exposed are firms selling to Chinese consumers and commodity exporters tied to Chinese construction. Weak domestic demand alongside strong exports tends to add to trade tensions with China's partners.
rubric_hit: Watch: property slump persists (real estate investment −21.6%, sales area −13.7% Jan–Oct); growth 4.6%, above the 3% line

sources.title: National Bureau of Statistics of China — National economy was generally stable in October

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
